headword: {弘法|こうぼう}も{筆|ふで}の{誤|あやま}り
reading: こうぼうもふでのあやまり
gloss: even experts make mistakes; even Homer nods

definitions.gloss: even experts make mistakes; even the skilled slip up; even Homer nods
definitions.explanation: A proverb meaning that even a master of a craft can make an occasional mistake. Literally, 'even Kobo Daishi makes brush errors,' referring to the famed calligrapher-monk Kukai (Kobo Daishi).

examples.japanese: {弘法|こうぼう}も{筆|ふで}の{誤|あやま}りだね。
examples.english: Even experts make mistakes, I guess.

examples.japanese: ベテランの{彼|かれ}がミスをするとは、{弘法|こうぼう}も{筆|ふで}の{誤|あやま}りだ。
examples.english: For a veteran like him to make a mistake — well, even the skilled slip up.

examples.japanese: {名人|めいじん}でも{失敗|しっぱい}することがある。{弘法|こうぼう}も{筆|ふで}の{誤|あやま}りというものだ。
examples.english: Even a master can fail sometimes. As they say, even Homer nods.

notes:
A well-known proverb. {弘法|こうぼう} refers to {弘法大師|こうぼうだいし} (Kobo Daishi), the posthumous name of the monk {空海|くうかい}, revered as one of Japan's greatest calligraphers. The point is that even such a master occasionally makes an error with the brush.

USAGE:
Used to comment forgivingly on an unexpected mistake by a skilled or experienced person — including oneself, with a touch of modesty or excuse.

SIMILAR PROVERBS:
- {河童|かっぱ}の{川流|かわなが}れ: even a kappa gets swept down the river
- {猿|さる}も{木|き}から{落|お}ちる: even monkeys fall from trees
